Common Questions

Things People Ask Before They Call

01

Do I need a permit for a screen enclosure in Florida?

Yes — screen enclosures are structural additions that require a building permit in Florida. We handle the entire permitting process for you, including plans, submission, and scheduling the final inspection.

02

How long does a pool enclosure installation take?

Most pool enclosures take 2–4 days to install once the permit is approved. Permit approval typically takes 1–3 weeks depending on your county. We'll give you a realistic timeline when we quote the job.

03

What type of screen do you use?

We stock standard 18×14 fiberglass screen, 18×16 no-see-um screen, Super Screen (heavier gauge, pet-resistant), and solar/privacy screen. We'll recommend the right mesh for your situation and exposure.

04

Will my HOA need to approve the enclosure?

Most HOAs require approval before any structural addition. We can provide design drawings and spec sheets to support your HOA application, and we've worked with dozens of communities across Central Florida.

05

How do I know if my existing enclosure is up to current wind load standards?

Enclosures built before 2004 may not meet today's Florida Building Code wind load requirements. We offer a free inspection and can tell you exactly where your structure stands and what — if anything — needs to be updated.
